text.p: Tropical Cyclone 07B has dissipated over South Central India. Heavy rains associated with the remains of the storm will continue for at least another 24 hours over the region. This system came from the Bay of Bengal and made landfall over eastern India, with Andhra Pradesh particularly hard-hit. The full extend of the damage will probably not be known for another day or two. We expect that the damage due to flooding, mudslides, a storm surge and very strong winds will be extemely high...especially in Andhra Pradesh.

Tropical Cyclone Melanie-Bellamine is a very powerful storm with 135 mph top winds. The storm threatens only shipping in the southern Indian Ocean. It is centered near 15s/76e and tracking to the south southwest. It is expected to pick up speed while turning to the south, slowly weakening.

Typhoon Dale is 130 miles southwest of Guam at this time, moving west northwest at 13 mph. Top winds are 105 mph and are expected to increase to over 150 mph during the next 48 hours, making the storm a major threat to shipping. It is no threat to land at this time.

Tropical Storm Ernie is moving west northwestward across the South China Sea, and may be a typhoon when it approaches Hainan, China, or northern Vietnam, by Sunday. This system is a threat to shipping.
